accepted.s: According to APSES 2025-26, Andhra Pradesh accounts for approximately what share of India’s total fish production?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh is estimated to contribute about 29% of India’s total fish production according to APSES 2025-26. The earlier estimate was about 30% in APSES 2024-25.
accepted.tq: Use the exact percentage and distinguish the latest figure from the earlier estimate.
accepted.sec: AP's rank - total fish, inland landings, shrimp and aquaculture, marine exports

accepted.s:
With reference to fisheries in Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. Andhra Pradesh had the highest inland fish landings in India in 2019-20.
2. Andhra Pradesh is the largest producer of farmed shrimp in India.
3. Vannamei is an important farmed shrimp variety in the State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Andhra Pradesh led India in inland fish landings in 2019-20 and is the largest producer of farmed shrimp, mainly Vannamei.
accepted.tq: Test the whole fisheries profile through a combination of rank, product and variety.
accepted.sec: AP's rank - total fish, inland landings, shrimp and aquaculture, marine exports

accepted.s: The fish and shrimp production of Andhra Pradesh in 2023-24 was approximately:
accepted.x: Production in 2023-24 was 51.58 lakh metric tonnes, against a target of 52.55 lakh metric tonnes.
accepted.tq: Match the production figure with the correct year rather than the nearby target figure.
accepted.sec: AP's rank - total fish, inland landings, shrimp and aquaculture, marine exports

accepted.s: In 2024-25, up to December 2024, Andhra Pradesh recorded fish and shrimp production of 41.38 lakh MT. This represented approximately what percentage of the target of 56.62 lakh MT?
accepted.x: The production of 41.38 lakh MT was 73.1% of the target of 56.62 lakh MT. The figure covered only nine months and did not indicate a fall in annual production.
accepted.tq: Calculate or recognise the stated production-to-target percentage and note the time-period qualification.
accepted.sec: AP's rank - total fish, inland landings, shrimp and aquaculture, marine exports

accepted.s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh recorded 9.64 lakh MT of fish and shrimp production valued at ₹24,345 crore in 2025-26?
accepted.x: West Godavari recorded 9.64 lakh MT of fish and shrimp worth ₹24,345 crore in 2025-26. Eluru, Krishna, Bapatla, Nellore, Konaseema and Kakinada are also important aqua districts.
accepted.tq: Use the district-value-production association as the identifying clue.
accepted.sec: AP's rank - total fish, inland landings, shrimp and aquaculture, marine exports

accepted.s: India is described as which one of the following in relation to global fisheries?
o: The third-largest fish producer and the largest shrimp importer
The largest fish producer and the leading marine-capture country
The second-largest fish producer but a minor inland-capture country
The second-largest fish producer and a leader in inland capture fisheries
accepted.x: India is the world’s second-largest fish producer, contributing about 9%, and leads in inland capture fisheries according to FAO SOFIA 2026.
accepted.tq: Separate the country’s global rank from its specific strength in inland capture.
accepted.sec: AP's rank - total fish, inland landings, shrimp and aquaculture, marine exports

accepted.s: By the end of 2018-19, Andhra Pradesh’s share in India’s seafood export value was approximately:
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh accounted for 36% of India’s seafood export value by the end of 2018-19. The later figures of 31% and 75% refer specifically to shrimp exports and cultured shrimp exports respectively.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the base of comparison—total seafood value versus shrimp-specific shares.
accepted.sec: Seafood exports - AP share, MPEDA, markets, tariff issues

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the later seafood-export shares associated with Andhra Pradesh?
o: 75% of India’s shrimp exports and 31% of cultured shrimp exports
31% of India’s total seafood exports and 75% of marine exports
31% of India’s shrimp exports and 75% of cultured shrimp exports
36% of shrimp exports and 60% of cultured shrimp exports
accepted.x: The later figures are 31% of India’s shrimp exports and 75% of India’s cultured shrimp exports. These percentages do not refer to all seafood exports.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similar percentages by identifying the precise export base.
accepted.sec: Seafood exports - AP share, MPEDA, markets, tariff issues

accepted.s: The Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA) functions as:
o: A regulatory body under the Ministry of Agriculture
The apex export body under the Ministry of Commerce
A financial institution under the Ministry of Finance
A research body under the Ministry of Environment
accepted.x: MPEDA is the apex export body under the Ministry of Commerce for marine products. Its arms include RGCA, NETFISH and NaCSA.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘which ministry or authority?’ method to distinguish the institutional mandate.
accepted.sec: Seafood exports - AP share, MPEDA, markets, tariff issues

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT an arm associated with MPEDA?
accepted.x: RGCA, NETFISH and NaCSA are associated with MPEDA. FIDF is the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund, not an arm of MPEDA.
accepted.tq: Find the one institutional term that does not belong to the MPEDA group.
accepted.sec: Seafood exports - AP share, MPEDA, markets, tariff issues

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (MPEDA-associated organisation)
a. RGCA
b. NETFISH
c. NaCSA

List-II (Association)
i. MPEDA arm
 ii. MPEDA arm
 iii. MPEDA arm

The correct combination is:
accepted.x: RGCA, NETFISH and NaCSA are all arms associated with MPEDA. The three organisations therefore correspond to the three MPEDA-arm entries.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure institutional association and eliminate codes that place an item outside MPEDA.
accepted.sec: Seafood exports - AP share, MPEDA, markets, tariff issues

accepted.s: Which country was the second-largest destination for India’s seafood exports in 2025-26?
accepted.x: China was the second-largest destination in 2025-26, with exports increasing by 20.1% by volume.
accepted.tq: Test the market ranking directly and avoid confusing it with the country on which exporters seek to reduce dependence.
accepted.sec: Seafood exports - AP share, MPEDA, markets, tariff issues

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India’s seafood markets in 2025-26:
1. Exports to China increased by 20.1% by volume.
2. Exports to the European Union increased by 35.2%.
3. Exports to South-East Asia increased by 28.2%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. China, the European Union and South-East Asia recorded the stated increases in seafood-export volumes in 2025-26.
accepted.tq: Check each market-wise percentage separately before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: Seafood exports - AP share, MPEDA, markets, tariff issues

accepted.s: The quantity and value of India’s seafood exports in 2023-24 were:
accepted.x: India exported 17.81 lakh MT of seafood valued at ₹60,523 crore in 2023-24. The figures of 17.35 lakh MT and ₹63,969 crore relate to 2022-23.
accepted.tq: Pair the quantity and value with the correct year instead of mixing adjacent rows.
accepted.sec: Seafood exports - AP share, MPEDA, markets, tariff issues

accepted.s: The marine fishing ban in Andhra Pradesh is imposed for how many days, generally from 15 April to 14 June?
accepted.x: The marine fishing ban lasts 61 days, covering the breeding season from 15 April to 14 June.
accepted.tq: Use the exact duration and dates as a linked numerical fact.
accepted.sec: Fishermen welfare - ban-period relief, diesel subsidy, insurance

accepted.s: The ban-period relief per fishing family from 2024-25 was:
accepted.x: The relief was ₹4,000 before 2019-20, ₹10,000 from 2019-20 and ₹20,000 from 2024-25.
accepted.tq: Arrange the changing benefit levels chronologically and identify the latest amount.
accepted.sec: Fishermen welfare - ban-period relief, diesel subsidy, insurance

accepted.s: During 2023-24, the Andhra Pradesh Government paid approximately what amount as ban-period relief to 1,16,613 fishers?
accepted.x: An amount of ₹116.613 crore was paid to 1,16,613 fishers during 2023-24.
accepted.tq: Match the beneficiary count with the associated expenditure figure.
accepted.sec: Fishermen welfare - ban-period relief, diesel subsidy, insurance

accepted.s: The ex-gratia assistance provided to the family of a deceased fisherman in Andhra Pradesh is:
accepted.x: Families of deceased fishermen receive ex-gratia assistance of ₹10 lakh. In 2024-25, ₹315 lakh was paid to 63 families.
accepted.tq: Distinguish individual family assistance from the aggregate amount paid to all beneficiaries.
accepted.sec: Fishermen welfare - ban-period relief, diesel subsidy, insurance

accepted.s: In 2024-25, ₹315 lakh was paid as ex-gratia assistance to how many families of deceased fishermen?
accepted.x: ₹315 lakh was paid to 63 families in 2024-25, with each family receiving ₹10 lakh.
accepted.tq: Use the aggregate-to-unit relationship to verify the beneficiary count.
accepted.sec: Fishermen welfare - ban-period relief, diesel subsidy, insurance

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding national support measures for fishers?
o: Group Accident Insurance covers 33.15 lakh fishers annually, and KCC has been extended to fishers since 2018-19.
Group Accident Insurance covers 3.315 lakh fishers annually, and KCC began in 2024-25.
Group Accident Insurance covers 63 lakh fishers annually, and KCC is restricted to marine exporters.
Group Accident Insurance covers 1.17 lakh fishers annually, and KCC was extended from 2019-20.
accepted.x: National Group Accident Insurance covers 33.15 lakh fishers annually, and the Kisan Credit Card facility has been extended to fishers since 2018-19.
accepted.tq: Check both the coverage number and the year attached to the credit facility.
accepted.sec: Fishermen welfare - ban-period relief, diesel subsidy, insurance

accepted.s: The fisheries cooperative structure in Andhra Pradesh comprises:
accepted.x: There are 2,356 fisheries cooperative societies with 3,09,018 members under the APCS Act, 1964.
accepted.tq: Retain the paired count of societies and members without reversing or altering the digits.
accepted.sec: Fishermen welfare - ban-period relief, diesel subsidy, insurance

accepted.s: India’s first Mega Aqua Food Park was operationalised at:
accepted.x: The Godavari Mega Aqua Food Park at Tundurru in West Godavari was India’s first operational Mega Aqua Food Park.
accepted.tq: Link the project title, location and district to avoid confusing it with other aqua infrastructure.
accepted.sec: Aqua infrastructure - mega aqua food parks, harbours, landing centres

accepted.s: The 10 fishing harbours in Andhra Pradesh, involving an outlay of ₹3,699.09 crore, are being implemented under:
accepted.x: The 10 fishing harbours are under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme component of PMMSY, not Sagarmala. The outlay is ₹3,699.09 crore.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct programme and reject the nearby infrastructure-scheme trap.
accepted.sec: Aqua infrastructure - mega aqua food parks, harbours, landing centres

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Upgrade of Kakinada fishing harbour — ₹178.51 crore
Modernisation of Visakhapatnam fishing harbour — ₹178.51 crore
accepted.x: Modernisation of Visakhapatnam fishing harbour has an outlay of ₹178.51 crore. Kakinada’s upgrade is ₹58.95 crore, the six Fish Landing Centres cost ₹126.91 crore, and the Integrated Aqua Park costs ₹88.08 crore.
accepted.tq: Match each project with its own outlay and eliminate swapped figures.
accepted.sec: Aqua infrastructure - mega aqua food parks, harbours, landing centres

accepted.s: The number of Fish Landing Centres planned or supported in Andhra Pradesh under PMMSY, with an outlay of ₹126.91 crore, is:
accepted.x: Six Fish Landing Centres are supported with an outlay of ₹126.91 crore. The figures 10, 12 and 35 refer to other infrastructure or planning categories.
accepted.tq: Separate the number of landing centres from harbours, aquaparks and aqua laboratories.
accepted.sec: Aqua infrastructure - mega aqua food parks, harbours, landing centres

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding aqua infrastructure in Andhra Pradesh?
o: The RGCA brood centre at Visakhapatnam is meant for Vannamei shrimp only.
Thirty-five Integrated Aqua Parks are already operational in Andhra Pradesh.
The Integrated Aqua Park is located at Parasavaripalem in Bapatla and has an outlay of ₹88.08 crore.
The Integrated Aqua Park is located at Tundurru in West Godavari and has an outlay of ₹126.91 crore.
accepted.x: The Integrated Aqua Park is at Parasavaripalem in Bapatla and costs ₹88.08 crore. Thirty-five Integrated Aqua Labs are planned, of which 30 are working; the RGCA brood centre at Visakhapatnam is for black tiger shrimp.
accepted.tq: Use location, project type and amount together to detect swapped infrastructure details.
accepted.sec: Aqua infrastructure - mega aqua food parks, harbours, landing centres

accepted.s: How many Integrated Aqua Labs are planned in Andhra Pradesh, and how many of them are working?
accepted.x: Thirty-five Integrated Aqua Labs are planned, of which 30 are working.
accepted.tq: Keep planned and operational counts in the correct order.
accepted.sec: Aqua infrastructure - mega aqua food parks, harbours, landing centres

accepted.s: Which of the following is proposed in connection with aqua infrastructure and export support in Andhra Pradesh?
o: A cold chain at Tundurru and a salt laboratory at Tirupati
A fish auction centre at Amaravati and a marine museum at Kurnool
A hatchery at Vijayawada and a tuna port at Anantapur
A chilling plant at Bhogapuram airport and an Aquatic Quarantine Facility
accepted.x: A chilling plant at Bhogapuram airport and an Aquatic Quarantine Facility have been proposed. The Aquatic Quarantine Facility is associated with MPEDA.
accepted.tq: Identify the proposal by connecting the facility with its relevant logistics and quarantine function.
accepted.sec: Aqua infrastructure - mega aqua food parks, harbours, landing centres

accepted.s: Under PMMSY, the total subsidy is what for the general category and women/SC/ST beneficiaries respectively?
accepted.x: The subsidy is 40% for the general category and 60% for women, SC and ST beneficiaries. The GoI-GoAP shares are 24%-16% and 36%-24% respectively.
accepted.tq: Read the categories in the same order as the question and do not reverse the percentage comparison.
accepted.sec: PMMSY and sub-schemes - PM-MKSSY

accepted.s: The Government of India and Government of Andhra Pradesh components of the 40% general-category PMMSY subsidy are respectively:
accepted.x: For general-category beneficiaries, the 40% subsidy consists of 24% from the Government of India and 16% from the Government of Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Split the total subsidy into its two stated government components.
accepted.sec: PMMSY and sub-schemes - PM-MKSSY

accepted.s: The implementation period and outlay of PM-MKSSY are:
accepted.x: PM-MKSSY covers FY 2023-24 to 2026-27 and has an outlay of ₹6,000 crore.
accepted.tq: Pair the scheme period with its own outlay rather than the larger PMMSY investment.
accepted.sec: PMMSY and sub-schemes - PM-MKSSY

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated feature of PM-MKSSY?
o: Compulsory replacement of all fishing boats with trawlers
Institutional credit for the fisheries sector
accepted.x: PM-MKSSY supports institutional credit, aquaculture insurance and supply-chain traceability. Compulsory replacement of all boats with trawlers is not a stated feature.
accepted.tq: Find the extreme and unsupported programme feature among the genuine objectives.
accepted.sec: PMMSY and sub-schemes - PM-MKSSY

accepted.s: The National Fisheries Digital Platform under PM-MKSSY had registered approximately how many stakeholders?
accepted.x: The National Fisheries Digital Platform had registered 30.60 lakh stakeholders.
accepted.tq: Retain the decimal placement and distinguish lakh from crore-scale figures.
accepted.sec: PMMSY and sub-schemes - PM-MKSSY

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with PMMSY results?
accepted.x: The reported PMMSY results include 28 fishing harbours and 2,195 Fisheries Farmer Producer Organisations (FFPOs).
accepted.tq: Match the two scheme-result counts without interchanging the categories.
accepted.sec: PMMSY and sub-schemes - PM-MKSSY

accepted.s: PMMSY results include how many Climate Resilient Coastal Fishermen Villages and Integrated Aquaparks respectively?
accepted.x: The reported results include 100 Climate Resilient Coastal Fishermen Villages and 12 Integrated Aquaparks.
accepted.tq: Distinguish infrastructure counts from village and organisation counts.
accepted.sec: PMMSY and sub-schemes - PM-MKSSY

accepted.s: The PMMSY allocation for 2026-27 and the FIDF corpus are respectively:
accepted.x: The PMMSY budget allocation for 2026-27 is ₹2,761.80 crore, while the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund corpus is ₹7,522 crore.
accepted.tq: Keep the annual allocation separate from the fund corpus and avoid reversing the pair.
accepted.sec: PMMSY and sub-schemes - PM-MKSSY

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about fisheries initiatives in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: 2,195 boat transponders were allotted, and the project began for three years from 2025.
7,522 boat transponders were allotted, and the project began for five years from 2026.
4,484 boat transponders were allotted, and a GEF-FAO aquaculture project began for five years from 2025.
4,484 boat transponders were allotted, and the GEF-FAO project began for five years from 2020.
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh allotted 4,484 boat transponders and has a GEF-FAO aquaculture project running for five years from 2025.
accepted.tq: Combine the correct quantity, project duration and starting year in one precise option.
accepted.sec: PMMSY and sub-schemes - PM-MKSSY

accepted.s: According to the available information on production composition, which statement is correct?
o: Marine and inland fisheries contribute exactly equal shares in India.
Marine fisheries account for more than 75% of India’s fish output.
Andhra Pradesh’s marine and inland shares are stated as exactly 50:50.
Inland fisheries account for more than 75% of India’s fish output.
accepted.x: India-wide, inland fisheries contribute more than 75% of fish output. A specific marine-versus-inland percentage split for Andhra Pradesh is not provided.
accepted.tq: Do not transfer an India-wide comparison to the State level when the State-specific split is unavailable.
accepted.sec: Marine vs inland production share in AP

accepted.s: The coastline of Andhra Pradesh according to APSES 2025-26 is:
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh has a coastline of 1,053 km according to APSES 2025-26. The older figure cited was 974 km.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the latest official figure from the older commonly cited figure.
accepted.sec: Coastline length
